name: Lab tests and mobile blood draw

pf.license.need: the lab's federal certificate for the kinds of tests it runs, and the state's lab license where the state requires one; a phlebotomist's certificate where the state requires one; collector training for drug tests (federal transport tests follow the federal collection rules); a doctor's order where the state requires one for a test
pf.license.who: both: the lab or draw business, and each phlebotomist or collector where the state's rules or the test's rules require it
pf.license.ask: optional, for the owner's own page: the lab's certificate number, the state license number, each phlebotomist's certificate; nothing is needed to book
pf.license.check: none: Rosie never looks up a license, certificate or training record; the owner keeps them current
pf.license.scope: only tests on the lab's certificate (tests sent on to a reference lab are named as sent out); a test needs a doctor's order unless the state's rules let the patient order it directly (a switch from the state form); a phlebotomist draws blood and collects samples, and never reads results or gives health advice
pf.license.blocks: none from Rosie: no booking is held or refused because a license can't be read
pf.license.renewals: none kept by Rosie: the owner keeps the renewal dates
pf.license.insurance: the owner's own liability insurance; Rosie never verifies it
pf.license.background: the practice's own background checks for phlebotomists who go into homes and care homes, where its rules or the state require them; Rosie never verifies them
pf.license.telehealth: none: a draw is always in person

pf.services.shape: clinic: a patient books a short draw slot at the patient service center (one of its draw chairs, staffed by whoever is on; nobody is booked by name), or a mobile draw at home, at work or in a care home; walk-ins wait in line for the next chair; tests come from a doctor's order or the lab's direct-to-you list; results come later
pf.services.examples: the example lab's own prices and lengths, not a standard

list.name: Blood draw with a doctor's order
list.price: billed to the health plan; self-pay from the lab's price list (example: basic metabolic panel $25, complete blood count $20)
list.after: the plan is billed; any share is billed after the plan pays
list.note: the doctor's order must be on file or brought along

list.name: Fasting blood test (cholesterol, glucose)
list.note: morning times only (the lab's setting, example before 10am); nothing to eat or drink but water for 8 to 12 hours, as the test says

list.name: Glucose tolerance test
list.note: fasting; a sweet drink, then draws over 2 or 3 hours; the patient stays the whole time; morning starts only

list.name: Direct-to-you test panel
list.price: example: wellness panel $79, vitamin D $45, A1C $35
list.note: only where the state's rules let a patient order the test; results go to the patient's secure page

list.name: Sample drop-off (urine, stool or a 24-hour collection)
list.note: the container is picked up before; walk in during drop-off hours

list.name: Mobile blood draw
list.length: 20 min at the place; a 2-hour arrival window in the morning
list.where: at the patient's home, workplace or care home
list.before: nothing taken (the visit fee billed after), or paid in full for a direct-to-you panel, or a card saved and charged at DONE
list.after: the bill after the plan pays, or the saved card
list.note: samples reach the lab by the courier's cut-off the same day

list.name: Employer drug test (urine)
list.where: at the patient service center, or at the workplace
list.after: billed to the employer its own way
list.note: photo ID and the chain-of-custody form; results go only to the employer's medical review officer, never through Rosie

list.name: Legal paternity DNA test
list.price: $350 (example) for the parent and one child
list.note: each adult shows photo ID and signs their own consent; a parent or guardian consents for the child; the chain of custody is kept

pf.services.capacity: draw chairs at the center (example 3), each a 15-minute slot; walk-ins fill open slots; mobile draws by route, a set number each morning; every sample must reach the lab within the time its test allows
pf.services.online: none: every draw is in person; results are on the secure page
pf.services.nobodyHome: never: the patient must be there
pf.services.walkIns: a line for the next open chair at the service center; booked times go first; sample drop-offs are checked in at once

date of birth (every sample is matched to the patient by two details)
medicines that matter for the test, like a blood thinner, only where the order asks

stop.words: chest pain, trouble breathing, fainting with an injury, or bleeding that won't stop

goOn.words: faints at the sight of needles, or fainted at a draw before

goOn.words: asks what a result means, or about a medicine
goOn.what: never answered by Rosie: the ordering doctor; for a direct-to-you test, the lab's own doctor service line

pf.safety.always: the generic screen: danger to life, fire, gas, a medical emergency → call 911, and no booking

steps.name: The doctor's order
steps.when: on file before the draw: the doctor's office sends it, or the patient brings it
steps.who: the lab gets it from the doctor's office when the patient hasn't got it

steps.name: Consent for a direct-to-you test
steps.when: signed on the secure page while booking
steps.result: signed: booked; not signed: no booking

steps.name: The plan check
steps.when: by the desk before the visit
steps.result: covered, part covered (the share shown), or not covered (self-pay or a free cancel); where the plan's rules require it, a notice of likely non-coverage is signed before the draw

steps.name: Fasting
steps.when: from the hour the test says, the night before

steps.name: A 24-hour collection container

steps.name: Employer drug test papers

steps.result: no ID: no collection; the employer's own rules decide what follows

pf.first_steps.prep: for the reminder: the fasting hours if the test needs them (water is fine), drink water, bring photo ID, the plan card and the doctor's order, and wear a short-sleeved shirt; for a 24-hour urine test, the container and the start time

pf.visit.checkIn: at the service center: the code at the desk, then photo ID and date of birth checked against the order (two details on every sample); mobile: the code at the door, then ID; a drug test: photo ID and the chain-of-custody form, watched only where the test's rules require it and then by a collector of the same gender
pf.visit.changes: the doctor adds a test to the order: drawn at the same visit if the samples allow, priced first for self-pay; nothing else is sold at a draw
pf.visit.cantGoAhead: no order, no ID, not fasting for a fasting test, the vein can't be found after two tries (the lab's limit), or the patient feels faint: the draw stops; a new draw is booked with no charge
pf.visit.done: the code, then DONE from the phlebotomist once the samples are labeled; the samples go to the lab by courier the same day; results go to the ordering doctor, and for a direct-to-you test to the patient's secure page; Rosie keeps only booking records
pf.visit.rejected: a sample the lab can't use (clotted, too little, too old): the patient is offered a new draw with no charge, by a secure link
pf.visit.dropOff: a sample container dropped off at the desk is checked in at once with the patient's two details

pf.money.before: doctor-ordered draws take nothing when booking; direct-to-you panels and paternity tests are paid in full when booking; a mobile draw takes nothing (its fee billed after), or a card saved and charged at DONE (the practice's setting)
pf.money.insurance: health plans: only the plan's name before times; member details on the secure page; the lab bills the plan after the samples are run; the patient's share is billed after the plan pays (Rosie texts the bill); a notice of likely non-coverage is signed before the draw where the plan's rules require it
pf.money.thirdParty: an employer pays for its drug tests on its own account, billed its own way; the employee pays nothing
pf.money.estimate: a self-pay patient gets a written price estimate before a scheduled test, where the rules require it
pf.money.caps: deposit cap: from the state form
pf.money.fees: no missed-visit fee at the service center; a mobile draw's visit fee may be kept for a late cancel or nobody home only if agreed when booking and the owner confirms; never for public-plan patients
pf.money.refunds: a direct-to-you test that can't be run and isn't drawn again: refunded in full

pf.messages.never: the test names, the order, results, health answers, medicines, ID numbers and plan details never go in a text: only the secure page; texts say only the lab's name, the day, the time and the place; a drug test or a paternity test is never named in a text
pf.messages.staffTexts: the owner and phlebotomists get the patient's initials, the time and the place; the tests are on the secure page
pf.messages.results: a text says only 'your results are ready on the secure page' (direct-to-you tests) or 'your results went to your doctor'
pf.messages.minors: a child's texts go to the parent or guardian

pf.staff.licenses: phlebotomy certificates and collector training, on the owner's own records (where the state requires them); Rosie never looks them up
pf.staff.skills: phlebotomy, children's draws, glucose tolerance tests, drug-test collection, paternity collection, mobile draws, Spanish
pf.staff.supervision: the lab director (the certificate holder) is responsible for the tests; a new phlebotomist draws under a trained one until signed off
pf.staff.oks: the owner OKs fees, refunds and free re-draws
pf.staff.standIn: any phlebotomist with the skill; nobody is booked by name; a drug test that must be watched only by a trained collector of the same gender
pf.staff.away: only phlebotomists cleared for mobile draws (with a background check where required) go to homes and care homes

pf.rules.privacy: a health privacy agreement (a business associate agreement) is signed before going live; health details only on the secure page
pf.rules.records: lab records and orders are the lab's own, kept as long as the federal and state rules require; never deleted on request while the rules say keep them; Rosie keeps only booking records
pf.rules.consent: direct-to-you testing only where the state's rules allow it, with consent on the secure page; drug tests follow the employer's program (federal transport tests follow the federal collection rules); legal paternity tests keep the chain of custody
pf.rules.showFacts: the lab's certificate shown where the rules require it; a notice of likely non-coverage where the plan's rules require it
pf.rules.results: results go first to the ordering doctor; a patient's own copy of a completed test is given on the secure page within the time the health privacy rules set
pf.rules.reviews: a rating may be asked; any reply never confirms the person was a patient

pf.edges.fasting: ate before a fasting test: the fasting part moves to another morning; no fee
pf.edges.noOrder: no doctor's order at the visit: the desk asks the doctor's office while the patient waits, or the draw moves with no fee
pf.edges.rejected: a sample the lab can't use: a free new draw
pf.edges.critical: a dangerous result: the lab's own process calls the doctor; never a text
pf.edges.faint: a patient feels faint or faints: the draw stops, the patient lies down, 911 if hurt; the owner is told
pf.edges.kids: a child is drawn with a parent or guardian there
pf.edges.mobile: a homebound patient doesn't come to the door: the phlebotomist calls, then the contact on the booking; the owner decides; no fee while the patient's safety is unknown
pf.edges.drugTest: an employer's drug test: the employee's own consent; results only to the employer's medical review officer
pf.edges.paternity: every adult consents for themselves; the child with a parent or guardian
pf.edges.results: results to the ordering doctor; direct-to-you results on the secure page
pf.edges.other: all other edge cases the generic way
